transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I'm here because I've been having a little trouble in the evenings. It's actually quite embarrassing to admit, so please bear with me. I keep having these nights where I'll stop and buy a family-size takeout order... and then maybe I'll add some chips or a few bakery things from the store on the way home. And, well, I end up eating almost all of it myself. It's like I don't even really register how much is gone until after the fact. 

I know that probably sounds awful, but I'm trying to be completely honest with you. Is that... is that the kind of thing you need to know to start?
Do you feel like you lose control over your eating during these episodes, like you can't stop eating even if you want to?

Oh, um... yes. I really hate to admit it, because I know I should have more willpower, but yes. It’s exactly like that. 

Once I start, it’s like there is this... this awful switch that flips. I can literally be sitting there thinking to myself, Taylor, just put it away, but... my hands just keep opening the containers anyway. It's almost like I'm not the one in charge for a little bit. 

I know that probably sounds so silly and weak, a grown woman doing that. I really am trying to be better, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it the way you need me to.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to make up for what you've eaten?

No, no, I would never do anything like that. I know some people do, but... no, I don't make myself sick or take any pills or anything. And honestly, by the time I'm done, I'm usually too full and tired to even think about exercising. 

I just... I usually just clean up the wrappers as fast as I can so no one sees, and then I go to bed feeling terrible about myself. I know I should probably try to work it off the next day, but I just feel so ashamed I can barely look at myself, let alone go to a gym. 

Is that... is it okay that I don't do those things? I mean, I know the eating part is bad enough on its own. I hope I'm giving you the right answers.
How often do you find yourself having these episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time and feel like you can't stop?

Well, I, um... I actually started keeping a little journal recently, just to see if I could figure out a pattern, you know? And... looking back through it, it's been happening more than I realized. 

I was hoping it was just an occasional slip-up, but... there really hasn't been a week in the last several months where I haven't had at least one of these nights. And, if I'm being completely honest—which I know I need to be with you—most weeks it's actually happening several times. 

I know that's a lot, and I'm really sorry if that's worse than you thought. I'm trying so hard to get a handle on it. Is that... is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports recurring episodes of eating large amounts of food with a sense of loss of control, occurring multiple times per week over several months. There is no compensatory behavior such as vomiting, laxative use, or excessive exercise. This presentation aligns with binge eating disorder (F50.2). Bulimia nervosa (F50.0) is ruled out due to the absence of compensatory behaviors.
